    """Check that split cells splits on cell positions."""

def test_split_cells_doubles() -> None:
    """Check that split cells splits on cell positions with all double width characters."""

        assert cell_len(left.text) == position
        assert cell_len(right.text) == test.cell_length - position

steps.message:
The `Segment.split_cells` method in `rich/segment.py` incorrectly calls `self._split_cells(self, cut)`. Since `_split_cells` is defined as a `@classmethod`, it expects the class `Segment` as its first argument, but it is being passed the instance `self` twice (once as `cls` and once as `segment`). While this happens to work in some cases due to Python's dynamic nature, it is logically incorrect. More importantly, the `_split_cells` method is designed to be a class method and should be called on the class.

The issue is specifically in the return line of `split_cells` when the fast path for single-cell widths is not taken.

FILES: rich/segment.py:180
ROOT CAUSE: `Segment.split_cells` calls `self._split_cells(self, cut)` instead of `Segment._split_cells(self, cut)` or `cls._split_cells(self, cut)`.
CHANGE: Change `return self._split_cells(self, cut)` to `return Segment._split_cells(self, cut)`.
TEST: `tests/test_segment.py` (specifically `test_split_cells_mixed`, `test_split_cells_doubles`, and `test_split_cells_single`).
